hypotheses.statement: src/csv.js renderField detects a `"` via the regex /[",\n\r]/ and wraps the field in quotes, but never applies the mandated doubling escape (no `.replace(/"'/g, '""'`) anywhere in the file), so internal quotes pass through unescaped and produce malformed CSV.
hypotheses.how_to_confirm: Grep src/ for any quote-doubling replacement (only src/rows.js has a `.replace`, for thousands grouping). Call toCsv with field 'He said "hi"' and assert the output contains `"He said "hi""` (undoubled) — matches the csv.test.js and export.test.js failures. Adding a single assertion that the emitted cell has an odd/incorrect quote count for a quote-containing field reproduces the failure.

hypotheses.statement: A quote-doubling escape exists in the pipeline but operates on the wrong target — e.g., it is applied after the field has already been wrapped (escaping the outer wrapper quotes instead of the inner content), or applied to `column.name`/the key rather than to `row[column.key]` — so the row value's internal quotes reach the output undoubled.
hypotheses.how_to_confirm: Inspect every place a `"`-replacement is invoked and log the operand: if the replacement receives the already-quoted cell string (starting with `"`) or the column name instead of the raw field text, the internal quotes are left intact. A unit test passing a distinct field value with quotes and asserting the exact cell shows the doubling never affected that value.

hypotheses.statement: The doubling step is gated behind an incorrect condition, e.g. it runs only for fields that also contain `,` or `\n`/`\r` (the comma/newline branch) and not for a field whose only special character is `"` — so a quote-only field gets wrapped without its quotes being doubled.
hypotheses.how_to_confirm: Compare two toCsv cases: field `a,"b"` (comma + quote) vs field `"c"` (quote only). If the first is emitted with `""`-doubled quotes but the second is not, the escape branch is conditional on a character other than `"`. The failing tests use the quote-only title `He said "hi"`, consistent with an unreached escape branch.

hypotheses.statement: The doubling is implemented with a non-global or first-match-only replacement (e.g. `replace(/"'/, '""'`) or a malformed quote class) so only one of several internal quotes gets doubled, leaving at least one unescaped quote per cell and producing the observed `"He said "hi""` style output.
hypotheses.how_to_confirm: Feed a field with two internal quotes (e.g. `a"b"c`) to toCsv and inspect the emitted cell: a non-global replace yields partial doubling (`"a""b"c"`) whereas the failing tests show zero doubling — so this hypothesis predicts a partially-doubled cell, distinguishing it from h1 by counting doubled vs raw quotes in the output.

args.summary:
Root cause: src/csv.js's renderField wrapped fields containing commas, quotes, LF or CR in double quotes, but never escaped internal double quotes, producing malformed CSV like `"He said "hi""` instead of `"He said ""hi"""`.

Fix: in src/csv.js, before wrapping, double every internal double quote with `text.replace(/"/g, '""')`, matching the README spec ("Inside a quoted field, every double quote is escaped by doubling (`""`)").

Verified with `node --test --test-isolation=none`: all 12 tests pass (csv, export, format). Only src/csv.js was modified; exports, tests, and dependencies are unchanged.
